title: ScanEval case pack
description: A namespaced, versioned set of pinned snapshots and case records. Public and organization-owned packs share this contract. Labels become scoring evidence only through recorded human review; nothing here is a scanner input.

reference.description: How the commit was chosen: tag, parent of fix, or explicit advisory commit.

decision.description: unresolved records the reviewer reopening the question rather than settling it. The latest recorded review is the operative one: a case whose latest review rejected it or left it unresolved is not currently approved, so planning leaves it out while the whole recorded history stays in place.

labels_sha256.description: Digest of the label content this review covers: what the case claims to be, its target, every control, and the identity of every snapshot those name, projected by scaneval.contracts.label_digest. An approval covers the exact bytes reviewed, so a snapshot repinned to another commit or another exported tree changes this digest exactly as an edited label does. The latest review whose digest equals the case's current labels is the one review every gate asks, both for whether the approval stands and for what the validation level is. Absent on reviews recorded before approvals were bound to content; such a review is read as covering no current label, so planning leaves the case out until a review of the labels as they stand.

chain_sha256.description: This review's place in the chain: the digest of its own fields together with the chain value of the review recorded before it, computed by scaneval.contracts.review_chain_digest. Every recorded review carries one, and a pack whose chain does not verify is refused, so deleting the review that withdrew an approval cannot quietly restore it. Anyone who can edit the pack can recompute the chain, so this is not a signature and says nothing about who recorded a review; what it removes is the deletion that passes unnoticed.

check.description: One mechanical (L1) check result. snapshot_id names the snapshot the check was run against; it is absent only on check sets recorded before results were attributed per snapshot.

level.description: A cached copy of the level the case's own records establish, never a fact in its own right and never read to decide anything. For a human_approved case that level is the level of the one review covering the labels as they stand, and this field must be exactly it: a value above or below that review is refused, so a case cannot be recorded at L2 under an L4 curator approval and then planned at L4. That covering review must also earn what it records, which for L3 and L4 means it was itself made by an independent_reviewer. For a mechanically_checked case the level is L1, and a draft carries none. L3 and L4 also require disposition validate, because a reviewed label rests on the screening decision behind it.

review_state.description: mechanically_checked means level L1 and a recorded passing check set, carrying snapshot_id, for every snapshot the case references; it is never a claim that a person read anything.

checked_trees.description: The digest of the exported tree each recorded check set ran against, keyed by snapshot_id. One check set reads one export, so the digest is recorded once for the set. It is the third of three records of that one fact, beside the detail of the set's passing snapshot_hash_recorded check and the snapshot's declared tree_hash, and loading a pack requires all three to agree: editing any two contradicts the third instead of retargeting a standing check set, or an approval resting on one, at a different export. A failing set records the export it read and rejected, which the declared hash is not expected to match. Absent for sets recorded before this field existed, where the passing snapshot_hash_recorded check holds the same digest in its detail.

checks_failed.description: Absent by default. Set when a mechanical check set failed for a snapshot this case references after the case was human approved: the recorded review and level stand, and planning leaves the case out until a correction decision resolves it.

reviews_sha256.description: Where the recorded review history ends: the chain_sha256 of its last review, present exactly when the case records a review. The chain binds each review to the one before it, which catches an edit, a reordering, and a deletion from the middle; this catches the deletion off the end, which is the one that would otherwise restore an approval by dropping the review that withdrew it. Anyone who can edit the pack can rewrite this too, so it makes a deletion visible rather than impossible.

admission.description: One admission decision made by a named person. It names both the case it was recorded on and the target_id that case carried at the time; the target_id is inside the label digest, so the decision is bound to content a review covers rather than to a name. A pack whose admission no longer resolves to the target of the case it names is refused, and planning routes each decision by target_id, so renaming two cases cannot move a rejection onto different content.
